_format: Shared types. Each key is a type name (PascalCase) that field types can use. docs/WRITING.md, 'The schema', describes every key. build.py makes one guide entry per type (id type-<name in lower case>).

EntityId.summary: A monster id or a character name.
EntityId.description: Monster ids are strings of digits (`++total_monsters + ""`, node/server.js:13417). A character's id is its name (node/server.js:11779). The server finds an entity by object key, so the number `48213` and the string `"48213"` find the same monster. `skill` (and so `attack` and `heal`) treats an id as a monster id when `"" + parseInt(id) === "" + id`, else as a character name (node/server.js:9903).

CharacterName.summary: The name of a character. It is also the `id` of that character.

InventoryIndex.summary: An index into `items` of the character: 0 to 41.
InventoryIndex.description: The inventory has 42 slots (`isize`, node/server.js:1456). Each field that takes an index says how the handler reads it. Some handlers use the value as an array key with no conversion. Then the string `"3"` works the same as `3`.

confirm.live_needed: The set of names is G.items, game data that the code does not fix.
The set of names is G.skills, game data that the code does not fix.
The set of names is G.maps, game data that the code does not fix.

InstanceName.summary: The instance that an entity is in. For a normal map it is the map name. A private instance has a random 24-character name.

confirm.note: Durations are computed (`expires - now`, timers), so they can have a fraction.

Milliseconds.summary: A duration in milliseconds. It can have a fraction.

confirm.note: `cache_item` copies every stored key except the ignored ones, so rarer stored keys can appear; the fields listed are those the code writes.

ItemInstance.summary: One item as the server sends it: an inventory slot, an equipment slot, or an item in an event.
ItemInstance.description: The server builds it with `cache_item`. It removes `grace, giveaway, gf, price, want, b, rid, list, o, oo, src` (node/server_functions.js:4190-4202, 4234-4261). A merchant stand slot keeps more fields (`price`, `b`, `rid`, `giveaway`, `list`); see `trade_sell`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The item. `"placeholder"` while an upgrade or a compound of this slot runs; see `PlaceholderItem`.

fields.name: q
fields.description: The quantity. Only for stackable items (`G.items[name].s`).

fields.name: level
fields.description: The upgrade or compound level. New items that can be upgraded or compounded get `0` (node/server.js:1986-1988).

fields.name: p
fields.description: A special property, for example `"shiny"`, `"lucky"`, `"glitched"`. A placeholder holds an object here. Can be `null`: a compound sets `item0.p = item0.p || item1.p || item2.p` even when no input had one (node/server.js:7073-7077), and the stored `undefined` comes back as `null`. Live captures show `p: null` on compounded rings, earrings, belts, amulets and orbs.

fields.name: stat_type
fields.description: The stat from a `pscroll`, for example `"str"`.

fields.name: l
fields.description: The lock state from `locksmith` (node/server.js:6820-6855). A locked item cannot be sent or upgraded with a `uscroll`.

fields.name: ld
fields.description: The end of the unseal wait: `JSON.stringify` of a `Date` 2 days in the future, so the string holds a quoted ISO 8601 date (for example `"\"2026-10-06T12:00:00.000Z\""`). `locksmith` `unlock` sets it on a sealed item (`l: "s"` becomes `"u"`) and reads it with `JSON.parse` on the next `unlock` (node/server.js:6819-6823). The server does not delete it when the unseal completes.

fields.name: m
fields.description: The merchant whose luck made the item.

fields.name: v
fields.description: A date string. The item came from PvP.

fields.name: acl
fields.description: Account locked: only characters of the same owner can get the item. The server tests it as true or false; the value type is unclear from the source.

fields.name: expires
fields.description: An ISO 8601 date string (a `Date` from `future_s`). The item expires at this time. The `elixir` slot always has it (node/server.js:7797-7799).

fields.name: gift
fields.description: The item was a gift. The value type is unclear from the source.

fields.name: skin
fields.description: A skin override.

fields.name: charges
fields.description: Charges of an item that skills use.

fields.name: data
fields.description: Free data of some items, for example a `cxjar`.

fields.name: ach
fields.description: The item achievement this item counts toward (a key of `G.achievements`); `item_achievement_increment` sets it and deletes it when the achievement completes (node/server_functions.js:5846-5868).

fields.name: acc
fields.description: The progress count of that item achievement. Deleted when the achievement completes (node/server_functions.js:5850-5865). Live captures show it without `ach` on some items.

fields.name: ex
fields.description: Only on the item in the `elixir` slot: `use` of an elixir sets `{name, expires, ex: true}` (node/server.js:7799). Renewing the same elixir keeps the object and only moves `expires` (node/server.js:7797).

fields.name: ps
fields.description: Every property the item has had, in order: `add_item_property` pushes the old `p` and the new one (node/server_functions.js:3220-3233). `cache_item` keeps it.

PlaceholderItem.summary: The item in an inventory slot while an `upgrade` or a `compound` of that slot runs.
PlaceholderItem.description: The server puts it in the slot of the item when the request succeeds. When the timer ends, the slot gets the result item. If the upgrade destroyed the item, the slot gets `null`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Always `"placeholder"`.

fields.name: p
fields.description: The state of the roll.

PlaceholderState.summary: The `p` object of a `PlaceholderItem`: the chance and the roll digits so far.

fields.name: chance
fields.description: The chance of success, 0 to 1.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The item that is in the upgrade.

fields.name: level
fields.description: The level of the item before the action. A compound always has it (`item0.level || 0`, node/server.js:7057); an upgrade copies `item.level`.

fields.name: scroll
fields.description: The scroll. `null` for an offering without a scroll. Absent from JSON when the value is `undefined`.

fields.name: offering
fields.description: The offering, if any: `offering && offering.name` (node/server.js:7059, 7449, 7555). `null` when the request's `offering_num` points at an empty slot; absent without `offering_num`.

fields.name: nums
fields.description: The digits of the roll that the server showed so far, 0 to 4 of them.

fields.name: success
fields.description: Set near the end of the timer when the result is a success.

fields.name: failure
fields.description: Set near the end of the timer when the result is a failure.

QueueEntry.summary: One timer in `q`, the queue of upgrade, compound and exchange actions of a character.

fields.name: ms
fields.description: The time left.

fields.name: len
fields.description: The full length of the timer.

fields.name: num
fields.description: The slot of the placeholder. It is the value from the request (`data.item_num` or `data.items[0]`) with no conversion, so a numeric string in the request stays a string here. `exchange` sets its own integer (node/server.js:6669).

fields.name: silent
fields.description: The server does not announce the result (a shiny attempt with an offering, node/server.js:7255).

fields.name: stale
fields.description: The character left the game while the timer ran (node/server_functions.js:4512).

fields.name: nums
fields.description: Only on a `compound` timer: always `[]` (node/server.js:7051). The server never fills it. The digits of the roll (0 to 9 each, up to 4) go in `p.nums` of the `PlaceholderItem` (node/server.js:14740-14798).

confirm.note: Each condition's other keys come from where it is added (`add_condition`, skills, encouragement); the type is open.

Condition.summary: One condition in `s` (a buff, a debuff or a state), keyed by its name.
Condition.description: Almost every condition has `ms`, the time left. `encouragement_lonewolf` has none: it is `{gold_multiplier: 3, xp_multiplier: 3, luck_multiplier: 3}` with no `expires`, and only a condition with `expires` gets `ms` (node/logic/encouragement.js:270-277). Many conditions have more fields, for example `f` (the character that caused it). The fields of each condition are in `G.conditions` and in the `skill` entry.

fields.name: ms
fields.description: The time left. Absent on `encouragement_lonewolf` (node/logic/encouragement.js:270-277).

confirm.note: `message(id, parameters, fields)` returns `Object.assign({}, fields, {message, phrase, phrase_args: parameters || {}})`: the three keys always exist, and `fields` cannot override them.

LocalizedText.summary: A text message in a form that the client can translate.

fields.name: message
fields.description: The English text.

fields.name: phrase
fields.description: The key of the phrase in the language files.

fields.name: phrase_args
fields.description: The values for the phrase; `{}` when there are none. `localization.message` always sets it (`parameters || {}`, languages/index.js:256-258), and so does the cavalry reply (node/logic/cavalry.js:237-239).

Hitchhiker.summary: An event that rides inside a `player` event: `[event name, payload]`.
Hitchhiker.description: The server adds these pairs to `player.hitchhikers`. The next `player` event carries them as `hitchhikers` and clears the list (node/server.js:4579-4581). The official client replays each pair as a socket event. Treat each pair as if the server sent that event.

GameResponseFailure.summary: The `game_response` object of `fail_response`: a request failed.
GameResponseFailure.description: `place` is the event name of the request, or the skill name for skills. The extra fields of each code are in the entry of the request that sends it.

fields.name: response
fields.description: The code. Each code has its own entry.

fields.name: place
fields.description: The event that failed.

fields.name: failed
fields.description: Always `true`.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: More detail for some codes.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: A copy of `request_id` from the request, on handlers that copy it.

GameResponseSuccess.summary: The `game_response` object of `success_response`: a request succeeded.
GameResponseSuccess.description: The extra fields of each code are in the entry of the request that sends it.

fields.name: response
fields.description: The code. `"data"` when the handler sends only data.

fields.name: place
fields.description: The event of the request.

fields.name: success
fields.description: `true`, or `false` when the handler sets it (for example `in_progress` work).

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: A copy of `request_id` from the request, on handlers that copy it.

Action.summary: One attack, heal or skill projectile, as `commence_attack` builds it.
Action.description: The same object goes to clients nearby as `action`, and to the attacker as the `game_response` result (with `response` and `place` added).

fields.name: attacker
fields.description: The id of the attacker.

fields.name: target
fields.description: The id of the target.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The skill, for example `"attack"`.

fields.name: source
fields.description: The same as `type`.

fields.name: x
fields.description: The position of the target at the start.

fields.name: y
fields.description: The position of the target at the start.

fields.name: eta
fields.description: Milliseconds until the hit: `floor(1000 * distance / G.projectiles[projectile].speed)`. Always present: the object starts with `eta: 0` (node/server.js:3546-3556), and an instant projectile keeps `0` and gets `instant: true` (node/server.js:3582-3586).

fields.name: m
fields.description: The map-change counter of the target.

fields.name: pid
fields.description: The projectile id, 6 random characters. The later `hit` carries it.

fields.name: projectile
fields.description: A key of `G.projectiles`. Always present: `commence_attack` reads `G.projectiles[def.projectile].speed` (node/server.js:3582-3583), which throws when it is `null`, so every sent `action` has one (node/server.js:3564-3565).

fields.name: instant
fields.description: The projectile has no travel time.

fields.name: damage
fields.description: The damage before the defenses of the target. Absent for a heal and for 0 damage.

fields.name: heal
fields.description: The heal amount, for a heal.

fields.name: positive
fields.description: The action helps the target (a heal or a buff).

fields.name: conditions
fields.description: Conditions that the hit can apply, for example `"poisoned"`, `"frozen"`.

fields.name: shield
fields.description: `shield_slam` only: `{name, level}` of the offhand.

fields.name: origin_offset
fields.description: Cavalry volleys only: the side offset of this shot in px, `-16` or `16` (`npc.volley_offset`, node/logic/cavalry.js:484; `0` is not sent, node/server.js:3562).

fields.name: response
fields.description: `commence_attack` adds it after it sends `action` to clients nearby, for the `game_response` to the attacker (node/server.js:3609). The server keeps the same object, so a reflected `action` also has it.

fields.name: place
fields.description: The same as `type`. Added with `response` (node/server.js:3610); a reflected `action` also has it.

fields.name: map
fields.description: The map of the attacker when the projectile hits. The server sets it at the hit (node/server.js:3733), so only a reflected `action` has it.

fields.name: in
fields.description: The instance of the attacker when the projectile hits (node/server.js:3734). Only a reflected `action` has it.

fields.name: reflect
fields.description: Only on a reflected `action`: the damage of the reflection, `ceil(attack * (0.9 to 1.1))`. The target reflected a magical attack (`reflection`), so `attacker` and `target` change places, `pid` is new, `x`, `y` and `m` are of the old attacker. `eta` keeps the value of the first action: the server does not change it (node/server.js:3775-3809).

Character.summary: The full state of your character, as `player_to_client` builds it.
Character.description: `player` sends it to its owner. With `stranger` set, the server leaves out the second group of fields (stats, inventory, gold) and uses it for other characters in `entities`. A field with the value `undefined` is absent from the JSON.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The name of the character.

fields.name: hp
fields.description: Hit points.

fields.name: max_hp
fields.description: Maximum hit points.

fields.name: mp
fields.description: Mana points.

fields.name: max_mp
fields.description: Maximum mana points.

fields.name: xp
fields.description: Experience in this level. Can be fractional: XP gains are not rounded, for example a merchant gets `tax * 3.2` per sale (node/server_functions.js:750); seen live as `106466429.2`.

fields.name: max_xp
fields.description: Experience for the next level.

fields.name: level
fields.description: The level.

fields.name: attack
fields.description: Attack value.

fields.name: heal
fields.description: Heal value (priests).

fields.name: frequency
fields.description: Attacks per second.

fields.name: speed
fields.description: Movement speed, px per second.

fields.name: range
fields.description: Attack range in px.

fields.name: armor
fields.description: Armor.

fields.name: resistance
fields.description: Resistance.

fields.name: x
fields.description: Position.

fields.name: y
fields.description: Position.

fields.name: map
fields.description: The map.

fields.name: in
fields.description: The instance.

fields.name: m
fields.description: The map-change counter. `move` must send this value.

fields.name: moving
fields.description: The character moves now.

fields.name: going_x
fields.description: The destination of the move.

fields.name: going_y
fields.description: The destination of the move.

fields.name: abs
fields.description: The position is absolute (after a teleport).

fields.name: move_num
fields.description: A counter of moves.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Set by cave logic on actors. Not set for a normal character.

fields.name: position_id
fields.description: Set for NPC characters. Not set for a normal character.

fields.name: motion
fields.description: Set for NPC characters with a scripted motion; `age` is its age in ms (node/server.js:857-858).

fields.name: s
fields.description: Conditions, keyed by name.

fields.name: c
fields.description: Channeled actions (for example `town`, `fishing`), keyed by name. Each has `ms`, the time left.

fields.name: q
fields.description: `player.q`: the timers of `upgrade`, `compound` and `exchange`, and the spins of the tavern `wheel` and `slots`, keyed by that name (node/server.js:6669, 7051, 7438; node/logic/tavern_wheel.js:27, node/logic/tavern_slots.js:54).

fields.name: b
fields.description: Unclear from the source; no handler sets it on a character.

fields.name: rip
fields.description: The character is dead. A gravestone cosmetic replaces `true` with its name (node/server.js:915-917). `false` after a revive or a state restore (node/server.js:1122, 6292, 15108); `null` is seen live on characters whose stored record holds it.

fields.name: afk
fields.description: `"code"` when the character logged in with `no_html` (a code client).

fields.name: controller
fields.description: Only when `afk` is `"code"`: the character whose code controls this one, or `""`.

fields.name: code
fields.description: The last `code` event said that code runs.

fields.name: target
fields.description: The current target.

fields.name: focus
fields.description: The focus target (`target` with `xid`).

fields.name: party
fields.description: The leader of the party. `null` after leaving a party (node/server_functions.js:3608, 3618, 3633): `player_to_client` copies any value that is not `undefined` (node/server.js:899-905).

fields.name: team
fields.description: The team in a team event.

fields.name: guild
fields.description: The guild: the guild's short name when the account is in one (node/server.js:11732, 11820-11823), else the character record's value, which is `""` or `null`. `player_to_client` copies it whenever it is not `undefined` (node/server.js:899-905), so `null` arrives (seen live).

fields.name: role
fields.description: A special role, for example `"gm"`.

fields.name: npc
fields.description: Set for NPC characters.

fields.name: allow
fields.description: Unclear from the source; no handler sets it on a character.

fields.name: pdps
fields.description: Party damage score.

fields.name: age
fields.description: The age of the character in days (node/server.js:11808).

fields.name: cid
fields.description: The change id. It goes up when the character changes.

fields.name: stand
fields.description: From `p.stand`: the merchant stand is open (the stand item name), or `false`.

fields.name: tp

fields.name: skin

fields.name: ctype

fields.name: owner

fields.name: encouragement

confirm.note: Every handler that reads a slot checks it with `in_arr(data.slot, trade_slots)`.

TradeSlotName.summary: A trade slot of a merchant stand: `"trade1"` to `"trade48"`.
TradeSlotName.description: The list is `trade_slots` (js/old_common_functions.js:52-53). How many of them are open depends on the stand and the class: see `get_trade_slots` (node/server_functions.js:4282-4299).

TradeSlotItem.summary: An item in a trade slot of a merchant stand, or an item in a trade `ui` event. It keeps the trade fields that `ItemInstance` removes.
TradeSlotItem.description: The server builds it with `cache_item(item, true)`, which removes only `grace`, `o`, `oo` and `src` (node/server_functions.js:4203, 4234-4261). A listing has `price` (a sale or a buy order) or `want` (a trade offer).

fields.name: price
fields.description: The gold for one unit. On a sale or a buy order. A giveaway has `price: 1` (node/server.js:7697-7699).

fields.name: b
fields.description: The listing is a buy order (`trade_wishlist`, node/server.js:8804-8809): the owner buys this item. A buy order always has `q`, also for an item that does not stack: `min(99, q)` for an upgrade or compound item, else `q` up to 9999 (node/server.js:8795, 8811-8816).

fields.name: want
fields.description: The listing is a trade offer: the owner gives the item for the item in `want`.

fields.name: rid
fields.description: A random id: 4 characters on a listing or a buy order (node/server.js:7710, 7753, 8807). An item bought from `secondhands` or `lostandfound` keeps its 5-character `rid` (node/server_functions.js:614, 645) until it is listed again. A new listing gets a new `rid`.

fields.name: giveaway
fields.description: The listing is a giveaway that lasts this many minutes.

fields.name: list
fields.description: The names that joined the giveaway. Only on a giveaway.

fields.name: registry
fields.description: Only on a giveaway that someone joined: the `auth_id` of each account that joined, mapped to the name of its character (node/server.js:8774-8776). `cache_item(item, true)` does not remove it, so the minute timer (node/server.js:16215) and `reslot_player` (node/server_functions.js:4308) send it to every client that sees the stand. A server bug: it leaks the `auth_id` of each participant.

fields.name: gf
fields.description: The item was won in a giveaway from this character (node/server.js:16121). `ItemInstance` removes it; the trade cache keeps it when the item is listed again.

TradeWant.summary: What a swap listing asks for in return: an item, the lowest level, a title and a quantity.
TradeWant.description: The server normalizes it with `trade_want_normalize`. `name` must be a key of `G.items` and not `placeholder`, else the listing fails with `trade_offer_invalid`. `level` stays only for an upgrade or compound item when `parseInt(level) > 0`, at most 12. `p` must be a key of `G.titles`; `null` or `""` means any title. `q` stays only for a stackable item: `min(G.items[name].s === true ? 9999 : G.items[name].s, max(1, parseInt(q) || 1))` (js/old_common_functions.js:479). An absent `level` or `p` accepts any. A `want` sent as a plain string is read as `{name: want}` (js/old_common_functions.js:471).

fields.name: name
fields.description: The item that the buyer must give.

fields.name: level
fields.description: The lowest level that the buyer can give, 1 to 12.

fields.name: p
fields.description: The title that the item must have, a key of `G.titles`.

fields.name: q
fields.description: The quantity of a stackable item.

BankPackName.summary: A bank pack: a key of `bank_packs`, `"items0"` to `"items47"`.
BankPackName.description: `bank_packs` (js/old_common_functions.js:54-102) maps each pack to `[bank map, gold price, shell price]`. `items0`-`items7` are on `bank`, `items8`-`items23` on `bank_b`, `items24`-`items47` on `bank_u`. A pack that you unlocked is an array of up to 42 items in `player.user`.

confirm.note: `home` is `player.p.home || region + server_name` (e.g. `"EUI"`); `resume.server` is `server_id.slice(3)`

CaveVisitInfo.summary: The daily visit state of the Cave of Many Dreams for your account.

fields.name: available
fields.description: `true` when the account has not used its daily opening.

fields.name: resets
fields.description: When the daily opening resets: a time in ms since 1970.

CallLogEntry.summary: One entry of the call-cost log of a socket: `[time, event name, cost]`.
CallLogEntry.description: `add_call_cost` keeps these in `socket.calls` and drops entries older than 4 s when the next cost comes. The time is a `Date` on the server, so it arrives as an ISO 8601 string. The name is the event of the handler, or a label that some costs use (`cm_data`, `bank`, `transport`). Each event starts a new entry with cost 1 (`add_call_cost(-1)`, node/server.js:4897). An extra cost with the same name as the last entry (from `CC`, or from `resend`) adds to that entry. The cost is a number and can have a fraction (`cm_data` to more than one target multiplies by 0.8, node/server.js:4930-4933). `reduce_call_cost` lowers the cost of the last entry and removes it at 0 or below. A cost of 0 or none counts as 1 (`if (!num) num = 1`, node/server_functions.js:5347-5349).

DropRow.summary: One row of a drop table: `[chance, what, ...]`.
DropRow.description: The first element is a chance. In `maps`, `drops`, `monsters_home_server` and `global*`, the entry drops when a random number divided by the luck factors is below it (node/server.js:2288-2370). In `tables`, it is a weight: one entry wins, with the chance weight / sum of weights (`exchange`, node/server_functions.js:4029-4149). The second element tells the kind. It is an item name, `"open"` (roll the table that the third element names), `"gold"`, `"shells"`, `"empty"`, `"cx"` or `"cxbundle"` (a cosmetic), or `"cxjar"`. For an item, the third element is the quantity and a fifth element is a property such as `"lucky"` (node/server_functions.js:4117-4119). `cxjar` is `[chance, "cxjar", 1, cosmetic]`. The forms in `design/drops.js` are exactly these.

TradeHistoryEntry.summary: One line of the trade history of a character: `[event, other character, item, price]`, plus the received item for a swap.
TradeHistoryEntry.description: `add_to_trade_history` writes it, at most 40 lines (node/server_functions.js:342-363). `buy` and `sell`: the price is the total gold of the trade, before the tax of the seller: the unit price (an integer, node/server.js:7682, 8808) times the quantity. `swap`: `["swap", partner, given, 0, received]`: index 2 is the item that the character gave, index 4 the item that it got. `giveaway`: only the giver records it, with the winner as the other character and no price (`undefined` in the array becomes `null` in JSON; node/server.js:16124, 16201). A trade can go into the last line (not for a swap). This occurs when the event, the other character, the item name and the level are the same. Then the server adds the quantity to `q` and the price to index 3.

TradeHistoryItem.summary: The item of a trade, in the trade view (`cache_item(item, true)`).

So a stand item keeps its `price`, `rid` and other trade keys (see `TradeSlotItem`). `q` is the quantity of this trade. The `sell`/`buy` lines of a buy order (`trade_sell`, node/server.js:8892-8894) copy the inventory item of the seller, so they have no `price`/`rid`.
